confidence_notes: Six web searches were run: one for the RBA rate and five for Havana prices. Searches gave aggregated figures, not venue-level checks. Sources: Numbeo, Hikersbay, Expatistan, a travel-cost aggregator and a few local news and guide pages. They disagree because of crowd-sourced data, mixed CUP, USD and CUC quotes, and the large gap between official and informal exchange rates. Numbeo-style data gave draft beer about $1.25-2.50, cappuccino about $1.1-1.9, an inexpensive meal about $6-7 and a mid-range dinner for two about $27.50. I set beer, coffee and meals slightly above those figures to reflect tourist-facing venues. No reliable direct price for cocktail or wine by the glass was found. Cocktail is based on tourist-bar mojito prices of about $5-8 in one guide. Wine is set at roughly twice the beer price, since a mid-range bottle was reported at only $4-10. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge: casa particular-style rooms, very few formal hostels, and state-run hotels. No accommodation searches or listing checks were done. Cuban prices are volatile and often quoted in USD or at informal exchange rates. The FX rate comes from a search result that cited the RBA exchange rates pages. I did not open the page myself.
comparable_city_reasoning: No close comparable. Prices are broadly in line with low-cost Caribbean and Latin American tourist destinations, but with a Cuba-specific USD-quoted tourist pricing layer. Food and drink are anchored on Numbeo-style Havana aggregates, adjusted up for tourist venues.
